newsitem.title: USA: Broward Cty, Fla., schools mull debt alternative.
newsitem.headline: Broward Cty, Fla., schools mull debt alternative.

text.p: Florida's Broward County School Board has agreed to review proposals by two municipalities to build their own schools and lease them back to the countywide district, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel said Wednesday.

Pembroke Pines has proposed issuing $35 million of muncipal bonds to finance three new schools. It has also offered to lend the school district $3 million to install portable classrooms at two other badly crowded schools in the city.
Miramar has proposed building two new schools, funded in part by money from housing developers, and asked the school board to cover interest payments on the debt.
The school board has agreed to informally consider the plans, and gave its staff until Feb. 11 to determine whether the proposals are financially and legally viable.

The school board had proposed putting a general obligation bond issue of $350 million to $800 million on the November ballot, but efforts to lobby for support stalled when polls suggested the measure had little chance of passing.
